title: What Happens When You Walk Into a Room and Forget Why?
description:
Send this to the friend who stands in the kitchen with no idea why.
In a 2011 Notre Dame study, people forgot more right after walking through a doorway than after walking the same distance inside one room, in 55 virtual rooms and in real ones. The researchers think a doorway works as an 'event boundary' that files the last room away, and going back to the first room didn't bring the memory back.
Next Body File: what happens if you sit all day.
Follow Body Files for a new one every day.

Sources:

BPS Research Digest, How walking through a doorway increases forgetting: https://www.bps.org.uk/research-digest/how-walking-through-doorway-increases-forgetting
Radvansky, Krawietz & Tamplin (2011), Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 64(8), 1632-1645, doi:10.1080/17470218.2011.571267
NHS, Why we should sit less: https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/exercise-guidelines/why-sitting-too-much-is-bad-for-us/
